extracted.intended_audience: Graduate students applying to the NSF GRFP (especially in ecology & evolutionary biology) and people seeking or contributing example GRFP statements
extracted.subtask_description: A curated repository of example Relevant Background & Future Goals (RBFG) and Graduate Research Plan (GRP) statements for NSF GRFP applicants, focused on ecology and evolutionary biology; also accepts contributor submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repository purpose — provide example RBFG and GRP statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Here are a set of example Relevant Background and Future Goals and Graduate Research Plan Statement statements for the NSF GRFP in Ecology and Evolutionary Biology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For ease of browsing a spreadsheet of these proposals is provided (link in README). The repository is intended as a model/sample collection; the author notes that models are likely similar across fields even though this collection targets ecology and evolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution format and filename guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Please email or submit a pull request if you would like to add your statements to this repo. Please send files as pdf, with as much information as you are comfortable including in the title, such as <something>.pdf, where <something> is RBFG (Relevant Background and Future Goals), GRP (Graduate Research Plan), or Reviews (share if you like).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit contributions as PDF files. Include in the filename an indication of the document type (RBFG, GRP, or Reviews) and any other identifying info you wish to share. Send via email or GitHub pull request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use external guidance/resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Many resources exist for guidance in writing a GRFP (see collected advice from Jennifer Wang, and Alex Lang, and proposals collected by Alex Lang).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the linked external resources and collected advice for writing the GRFP. The README suggests that although this repo focuses on ecology/evolution, the models/examples likely apply across fields; users are invited to send additional links.
